This page documents a [[id:31C868B9-306E-4282-BA8C-07E647021B34][task]] in the [[id:079FA16E-82FB-45AB-AA1C-A8BDF43B7E40][Keep the nightly include-cleaner out of generated files]] story. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance, and any notes or results.

* Goal

Every include fix from the nightly run lands in the layer that owns the file: hand-crafted sources directly, generated sources through their templates.

* Status

| Field        | Value                                  |
|--------------+----------------------------------------|

| Last touched | 2026-10-07                               |

* Acceptance

- The changes in PR #2738 are classified as generated or hand-crafted, with the method recorded.
- The nightly fixer leaves generated files alone and reports them instead.
- The sound hand-crafted fixes land and the unsound suggestions are dropped.

* Plan

The method, in the order that settles each file:

1. List the run's files with =git diff --name-only origin/main...origin/bot/nightly-includes=.
2. Mark each by the marker the codegen writes into every output it produces: =AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY=, emitted for C++, CMake and org by =core.py=.
3. Cross-check against the generator itself. =codegen.py regenerate --component refdata --address ores.cpp --dry-run= lists the files the models produce, and =check_component_drift.py --component refdata --dry-run= proves the checked-in generated tree still matches its templates.
4. Reject any suggestion that names an implementation header where a public one exists.

/Result./ All 49 files are hand-crafted. None carries the marker, none appears in the generator's output list, and applying the whole patch leaves the refdata drift gate clean — so this run needs no archetype change. The codegen half of the problem is therefore preventative: the fixer scanned 5115 generated translation units of 6183, and a future run will find one of them include-dirty and edit output that the next regeneration overwrites.

=check_includes.sh= now removes the marked files from the clang-tidy list and prints each one on stderr. A generated file with an include problem is fixed in its =ores.*.org= archetype, re-tangled with =compass build --direct tangle_codegen_templates= and regenerated.

* Notes

The 49 files split into three kinds of change. Most are plain missing direct includes: =<string>=, =<vector>=, =<cstdint>=, =<optional>=, =<utility>=, =<chrono>= and the project headers the file's own symbols come from. Some narrow an umbrella include to the headers actually used, and those are sound: =options.cpp= keeps only =<rfl/json/write.hpp>= because it calls only =rfl::json::write=, and =parser.cpp= keeps =errors.hpp= and =options_description.hpp= because it names only =boost::program_options::error= and =options_description=.

Four suggestions name implementation headers and were dropped:

- =<bits/chrono.h>=, a libstdc++ internal, alongside the =<chrono>= the same hunk adds.
- =<boost/asio/impl/co_spawn.hpp>=, swapped in for =<boost/asio/co_spawn.hpp>= in two files.
- =ores.service/service/domain_service_runner_impl.hpp= and
  =host_runner_impl.hpp=, swapped in for the public headers. Both public
  headers include their =_impl= at the end, so the public include is
  sufficient and is the interface to keep.

The codegen question the story was opened for turned out to have no
present-day instance: nothing in this run needed a template change. The
guard is what keeps it that way.
